 Kohima, Nov 11: Kohima is set to witness three weeks of competitive football as 22 teams prepare to vie for the 26th NSF Martyrs’ Memorial Trophy 2026, beginning November 13 at the Indira Gandhi (IG) Stadium.
 Organised by the Angami Students’ Union (ASU) under the aegis of the Naga Students’ Federation (NSF), the tournament will continue until December 3, with a total prize pool of Rs. 8.8 lakh. The grand finale is scheduled for December 3 at 4 PM.
 The tournament, one of Nagaland’s recognised football competitions, will bring together football clubs, academies and youth organisations from across the region. The 22 participating teams have been divided into two pools of 11 teams each.
 Pool A comprises New Market FC, D’ Block Youth Organisation, Ward-19, Mez & Co FA, Kidima Farmers United, Lamkang Student’s Union, KPMT, United Brother’s FC, Tiseru FC Meriema, Corinthians FC and All Zeliangrong Students’ Union.
 Advertisement Pool B features Headhunters FC, Chüziena FC, Y.O Bros FC Phezoucha, Legacy FC, United-4 FC Kohima, Anal Lenruwl Tangpi, Luminous FC, Medziphema Football Academy, Asüfü Football Academy, Nerhema FC and SZFC Academy.
 The tournament will follow a competitive knockout format, with the semi-finals scheduled to be played on a double-leg basis. Teams will compete for the championship title and a share of the Rs. 8.8 lakh prize money.
 The champions will receive Rs. 3.5 lakh, while the runners-up will take home Rs. 2 lakh. The losing semi-finalists will be awarded Rs. 60,000 each, and the losing quarter-finalists Rs. 30,000 each.
 Individual performances will also be recognised through awards of Rs. 10,000 each for Best Custodian, Best Defender, Best Midfielder, Golden Boot, Fair Play and Most Promising Player (Under-19). The Player of the Tournament will receive Rs. 30,000, while Player of the Match awards will be presented after every game.
 Beyond the sporting contest, the NSF Martyrs’ Memorial Trophy carries a legacy of remembrance. The tournament honours Lt. Kekuojalie Sachü of Kohima Village and Lt. Vikhozo Yhoshü of Kigwema Village, who were killed on March 20, 1986, when armed police personnel opened fire on students at Alichen in Mokokchung during a protest organised by the NSF.
 The students were protesting against the proposed extension of the Disturbed Area Belt from five to 20 kilometres along the Indo-Myanmar border and the induction of Indian Police Service (IPS) cadres into Nagaland.
 The deaths of the two students became a defining moment in the history of the Naga students’ movement. March 20 is observed annually as NSF Martyrs’ Day in their memory.
 The football tournament traces its origins to a competition among the four ranges of the Angami Students’ Union — Northern, Western, Southern and Chakhro — held during the late 1980s until 1991.
 In 1992, the competition was opened to teams beyond the four ranges under the banner of the Open NSF Martyrs’ Trophy. It was subsequently renamed the NSF Martyrs’ Memorial Trophy in 1998.
